# PaperMind

> Upload a research paper or an arXiv ID and get a full-paper summary, its numbers and tables, and a knowledge graph linking it to the rest of your library.

**895/895 citations verified** against the code at `fcb26da` on 2026-11-06. Generated by [Onramp](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/onramp).

PaperMind reads a whole research paper (a PDF you upload, or one fetched from arXiv) and stores a structured account of it: an analysis of roughly 800-1200 words, key findings that carry the paper's own numbers, contributions, limitations, future work, the tables and figures, and typed entities (methods, materials, measurements, tools). Every paper goes into your personal library, where similarity search and a knowledge graph connect it to papers you already have, and an on-demand layer adds a simulated peer review, research gaps, a reproducibility score and a slide deck.

It is built for people who read many papers and want to keep what each one measured. It runs on free LLM tiers: Gemini first, Groq second, a local Ollama model last.

*In one picture:* PaperMind is a library intake desk. You hand in a paper and get a ticket (a row in `processing_jobs`). A team in the back room reads it, writes a report and shelves it next to related papers, while a board at the front (the processing tray) shows which tickets are done. Unlike a real desk, the back room refuses to shelve a blank or placeholder report: a failed reading comes back as a failed ticket, not as a thin summary.

## The gist

### What PaperMind does

*core · 4 min*

**In short:** You give PaperMind a PDF or an arXiv ID; it reads the whole paper with an LLM and stores a structured account of it in your library, linked to related papers.

Picture the job a careful reader does after finishing a paper: write a page on what it did, list the headline numbers, note the limitations, copy out the key tables, and file it next to related work. PaperMind does that job and keeps the result.

For each paper it stores, in one database row:

- a long analysis, with separate write-ups of the method and the experimental setup. The schema asks the model for 800-1200 words and for findings that each carry a number from the paper ([`core/graph/schemas.py:99-103`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/schemas.py#L99-L103));
- entities in four kinds that work outside machine learning: method, material, measurement, tool ([`core/graph/schemas.py:24`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/schemas.py#L24));
- the tables and figures lifted out of the PDF;
- a per-stage `ok`/`failed` record, so 'nothing found' and 'this step crashed' look different.

Around the library sit features you call on demand: a knowledge graph of similar papers, semantic search, a timeline, a simulated peer review, research gaps, a reproducibility score and a slide deck. They are ordinary HTTP routes, 76 in all, mounted in one place ([`backend/main_app.py:62-98`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L62-L98)).

Two design choices shape everything else. It runs on **free LLM tiers**, Gemini first, Groq second, a local Ollama model last, so it is built to survive rate limits. And it **refuses to store a failure as a result**: a run that cannot produce a real summary becomes a failed job, not a plausible-looking paragraph.

> **Checkpoint:** A friend uploads a clinical trial paper. Which part of PaperMind's output is designed so that it still works outside machine learning?
> - The regex entity extractor's list of models and datasets
> - The four entity kinds: method, material, measurement, tool
> - ROUGE scoring against the abstract
> - The slide deck export
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The four entity kinds: method, material, measurement, tool. The graph engine's schema uses domain-neutral kinds on purpose ([`core/graph/schemas.py:8-12`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/schemas.py#L8-L12)); the regex extractor only knows ML names.</details>

### The mental model: a ticket, a back room, a shelf

*core · 5 min*

**In short:** An upload creates a job row; a worker inside the API process claims it and runs agents plus an LLM graph; the result is one `summaries` row; the browser polls to find out.

Hold one picture in your head and most files will make sense: **a ticket, a back room, a shelf**.

1. **The ticket.** When you upload, the API does not process anything. It checks the file, saves it to disk and inserts a row in `processing_jobs`, then answers 202 within a second ([`backend/routes/process_jobs.py:162-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/process_jobs.py#L162-L185)).
2. **The back room.** Each API process runs a `JobWorker` that claims queued rows from the database ([`backend/services/job_queue.py:94-127`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L94-L127)). For a claimed job it runs the pipeline: extract the PDF into sections, run ten agents, run the LangGraph summary engine, check the result.
3. **The shelf.** A passing result becomes one row in `summaries`, with everything in a JSON column, plus rows in the graph tables (similar papers, citations).
4. **The board.** The browser polls `GET /api/process/jobs` every 2 seconds while something runs and shows a tray; when a job turns `succeeded` it clears its caches and the new paper appears ([`frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js:96-101`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js#L96-L101)).

Everything else (graph, search, peer review) reads from the shelf.

Where the picture stops working: the back room is not a separate service. The worker lives inside the same Uvicorn process that answers HTTP requests, and coordination between processes happens entirely through the database.

> **Checkpoint:** You upload a PDF and the API answers in under a second. What has happened by then?
> - The summary has been generated and saved
> - A job row was inserted and the PDF staged on disk; nothing has been processed yet
> - The PDF was sent to Gemini
> - The PDF has been split into sections
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>A job row was inserted and the PDF staged on disk; nothing has been processed yet. The enqueue route only validates, stages the file and inserts the job ([`backend/routes/process_jobs.py:144-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/process_jobs.py#L144-L185)); a worker does the rest later.</details>

## Run it

### Run it on your machine

*core · 5 min*

**In short:** You need a Supabase project with the schema loaded, one LLM key (or Ollama), the API on port 8000 and the Vite dev server on port 3000.

Four things must exist before a paper can be processed: Python dependencies, a configured `backend/.env`, a database with the schema, and at least one LLM.

**Install.** One venv, two requirement files: the root one for the pipeline (PyMuPDF, pymupdf4llm, LangGraph, the LangChain provider packages) and `backend/requirements.txt` for the web server ([`backend/requirements.txt:1-5`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/requirements.txt#L1-L5)).

**Configure.** Copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and set `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`, a 32+ character `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GROQ_API_KEY`. Startup checks the first three and lists what is wrong; in production it refuses to start ([`backend/main_app.py:105-113`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L105-L113)).

**Database.** Run `schema.sql`, `experience_schema.sql`, then every file in `migrations/` in order, in the Supabase SQL editor. Several functions the code calls (`match_papers`, `claim_processing_job`) only exist after that.

**Start.** `cd backend && uvicorn main_app:app --reload --port 8000`, then `cd frontend && npm run dev`. Vite forwards `/api` to port 8000 ([`frontend/vite.config.js:7-14`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/vite.config.js#L7-L14)).

**Check.** `/api/health/ready` reports the database; `/api/health?probe_llm=true` sends a one-word prompt to each provider. Sign up, drop a PDF on the home page and watch the tray.

Without any key, the chain is Ollama alone, which needs `ollama serve` and the two Qwen models pulled ([`core/llm/providers.py:59-63`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L59-L63)).

> **Checkpoint:** The API starts, but the log repeats `job_claim_failed` every few seconds with an error saying a function does not exist. What did you skip?
> - Installing the frontend
> - Running the SQL migrations in Supabase
> - Setting REDIS_URL
> - Pulling the Ollama models
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Running the SQL migrations in Supabase. `claim_processing_job` is a Postgres function created by the migrations; the repository only calls it ([`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:62-74`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L62-L74)).</details>

### Configuration is read two ways

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** The backend reads `.env` into a typed `Settings` object; most of `core/` reads `os.environ` directly. `core/__init__.py` loads `.env` into the environment so both see the same values.

Two pieces of code read your configuration, and they read it differently.

`backend/config/settings.py` declares every backend setting as a typed field on a pydantic-settings class that reads `backend/.env` ([`backend/config/settings.py:22-30`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L22-L30)). Routes get it through `get_settings()`, cached once per process.

Most of `core/` is older than that class and calls `os.environ.get(...)` directly: the provider chain reads `PAPERMIND_LLM_PROVIDER` and the API keys this way ([`core/llm/providers.py:101-112`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L101-L112)). pydantic-settings does **not** copy what it reads from `.env` into `os.environ`. Without a bridge, `core/` would silently see no keys and fall back to Ollama.

The bridge is `core/__init__.py`, which loads `backend/.env` into the real environment the first time anything under `core` is imported ([`core/__init__.py:11-27`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/__init__.py#L11-L27)). It uses `override=False`, so a variable already set in your shell wins over the file.

Two rules follow:

- A value `core/` reads must be **in `.env`** (or the shell), not only a default on `Settings`. `Settings` declares `papermind_llm_provider = 'auto'` ([`backend/config/settings.py:96-105`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L96-L105)), but `core/` never sees that default.
- Some settings are dead. `PAPERMIND_USE_GRAPH` is declared and set in Compose, but no code reads it: the graph engine is always on.

The same file also forces UTF-8 on stdout and stderr, because a Windows console logging a '≥' from a paper used to crash the summariser ([`core/__init__.py:30-47`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/__init__.py#L30-L47)).

> **Checkpoint:** You set `GROQ_API_KEY` only as a default value in the `Settings` class and leave it out of `backend/.env`. What happens to summaries?
> - Groq is used, because Settings is the single source of truth
> - The provider chain never sees the key and falls back to the providers it can find, ending with Ollama
> - The app refuses to start
> - FastAPI copies Settings into os.environ at startup
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The provider chain never sees the key and falls back to the providers it can find, ending with Ollama. The chain checks `os.environ` ([`core/llm/providers.py:105-112`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L105-L112)), and only `.env` values are copied there by `core/__init__.py`.</details>

### Docker, CI and the checks you can run

*deep · 5 min*

**In short:** Compose runs api, web and redis behind nginx on port 8080; CI runs pytest with a 45% coverage floor and a golden-set quality gate that needs no API key; `npm run smoke` loads every page in a real browser.

**Compose.** `docker compose up --build` starts three services. `api` is the FastAPI image with 2 Uvicorn workers by default, each running its own job worker ([`backend/Dockerfile:74-76`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/Dockerfile#L74-L76)). `web` is nginx serving the built frontend and proxying `/api` with a 600-second read timeout ([`frontend/nginx.conf:42-45`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/nginx.conf#L42-L45)). `redis` runs with persistence off and a 256 MB LRU cap, because everything in it can be rebuilt ([`docker-compose.yml:74-84`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/docker-compose.yml#L74-L84)). Uploads live on a named volume so they survive a container swap.

**Tests.** `tests.yml` installs all three requirement files and runs `pytest tests/` with `--cov-fail-under=45` ([`.github/workflows/tests.yml:27-29`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L27-L29)). Run it from the venv: a system Python lacks `langgraph` and reports dozens of collection errors.

**Quality gate.** `evals.yml` downloads each labelled paper from arXiv, validates the golden set and runs `golden_eval.py gate` ([`.github/workflows/evals.yml:38-51`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/.github/workflows/evals.yml#L38-L51)). Grounding and section detection need only a local embedding model, so the gate runs on every PR, forks included.

**Frontend.** `npm run lint` allows zero warnings; `npm run smoke` drives Chromium through every route and fails on any console error or error boundary ([`frontend/scripts/smoke.mjs:29-41`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/scripts/smoke.mjs#L29-L41)). It needs the dev server and the API running.

**Health.** `/api/health/live` says the process is up, `/api/health/ready` says the database answers, `/api/health` adds Redis, the worker and, with `?probe_llm=true`, a live call to each provider.

## The stack

### The stack at a glance

*core · 3 min*

**In short:** Python 3.11 with FastAPI, LangGraph and PyMuPDF on the back; React 18 with Vite and Tailwind on the front; Supabase Postgres with pgvector for storage; Redis optional.

Read the table below once; each row says what the technology does **here**, not in general. Three groupings help:

- **Serving requests:** FastAPI on Uvicorn, Pydantic for request bodies and settings, PyJWT and bcrypt for accounts, structlog for logs ([`backend/main_app.py:133-141`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L133-L141)).
- **Reading papers:** PyMuPDF and pymupdf4llm turn PDFs into Markdown sections; LangGraph runs the summary engine; LangChain's Gemini, Groq and Ollama clients make the LLM calls; sentence-transformers computes embeddings locally ([`core/llm/providers.py:41`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L41)).
- **Showing results:** React 18 pages lazy-loaded by React Router, an axios client, Tailwind with design tokens, d3-force for the graph.

Storage is one Supabase Postgres database. The backend uses the service-role key, which bypasses row-level security, so ownership checks are the code's job.

If any row is new to you, the primers in this chapter (marked for newcomers) give you enough to read the code.

### Primer: FastAPI, async and to_thread

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Handlers are `async`, dependencies are injected with `Depends`, and every blocking call (Supabase, PyMuPDF, embeddings) is pushed onto a thread with `asyncio.to_thread`.

A FastAPI route is a decorated function. Its parameters say what it needs: a body model, a path value, or a dependency. `CurrentUser` is a dependency: FastAPI calls `get_current_user` first, which reads the Bearer header or cookie and returns the token payload or raises a 401 ([`backend/auth/dependencies.py:14-44`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/dependencies.py#L14-L44)). `SummaryRepoDep`, `JobRepoDep` and `SettingsDep` work the same way ([`backend/api/deps.py:33-34`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/api/deps.py#L33-L34)).

Handlers here are `async def`. An async function runs on one event loop thread that juggles many requests, switching whenever one of them `await`s. That only works if nothing blocks the loop. Three things in this codebase block:

- the Supabase Python SDK (synchronous HTTP),
- PDF extraction and table detection (CPU and a subprocess),
- embedding with sentence-transformers (CPU).

So you see `await asyncio.to_thread(fn, ...)` everywhere: it runs `fn` on a worker thread and lets the loop continue. The base repository does it for every query ([`backend/repositories/base.py:43-55`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/base.py#L43-L55)), and StructureAgent does it for extraction because a slow paper could otherwise freeze every other request for minutes ([`core/agents/structure_agent.py:80-88`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/structure_agent.py#L80-L88)).

One consequence: a single Supabase client used from many threads corrupted its HTTP/2 connection, so the provider now gives each thread its own client ([`backend/db/client.py:22-36`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/db/client.py#L22-L36)).

When you add code to a route, ask: does this call block? If yes, wrap it.

### Primer: LangGraph and structured output

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** LangGraph runs functions (nodes) over one shared dict (state) along declared edges; LangChain's `with_structured_output` makes the model fill in a Pydantic class.

A LangGraph graph is a flowchart you can run. You give it:

- a **state** type, here `SummaryState`, a dict with keys such as `sections`, `digests`, `synthesis`, `grade` ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:96-115`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L96-L115));
- **nodes**, async functions that receive the state and return only the keys they change. `prepare` returns `chunks`, `paper_text`, `single_pass` and `attempts`;
- **edges**, including conditional ones that call a small function to choose the next node.

`get_summary_graph` is the whole control flow in 30 lines ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:627-661`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L627-L661)). Read it before any node. Two edges out of `map_sections` mean the two extract nodes run in parallel; two edges into `synthesize` mean it waits for both. The edge from `grade` back to `synthesize` is the retry loop.

Each node that talks to an LLM uses **structured output**: `model.with_structured_output(PaperSynthesis)` sends the class's JSON schema with the request and parses the answer back into the class, raising if it cannot ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:140-157`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L140-L157)). That raise matters: it is what makes `with_fallbacks` move on to the next provider.

Because the schema travels with the request, **the field descriptions in `schemas.py` are prompt text**. Changing 'Up to ~25' to 'Up to ~50' changes what the model returns, which is why a prompt fingerprint and an eval gate exist.

> **Checkpoint:** In the summary graph, what makes `synthesize` wait until both entity and result extraction are done on the map-reduce path?
> - An explicit asyncio.gather inside synthesize
> - Two edges into synthesize, one from each extract node
> - A lock in the provider chain
> - The semaphore in _structured
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Two edges into synthesize, one from each extract node. LangGraph waits for every incoming edge: [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:648-653`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L648-L653).</details>

### Primer: Supabase, JSONB and pgvector

*standard · 4 min*

**In short:** Supabase is hosted Postgres with a REST layer; the code builds queries with a fluent client, calls SQL functions with `.rpc`, stores pipeline output as JSONB and embeddings as pgvector columns.

Supabase gives you a Postgres database plus PostgREST, a server that turns HTTP calls into SQL. The Python client hides the HTTP: `supabase.table('summaries').select('id').eq('user_id', uid).execute()` becomes a `SELECT ... WHERE user_id = ...`. Server-side SQL functions are called by name with `.rpc(name, params)`, as the job queue does for `claim_processing_job` ([`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:62-74`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L62-L74)).

Two Postgres features carry this app:

- **JSONB**: a column holding a JSON document that Postgres can index and query. `summaries.summary_data` holds the whole pipeline output. The arrow syntax selects inside it, so the graph builder reads only the `entities` key of 80 papers instead of 80 full documents ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:184-198`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L184-L198)).
- **pgvector**: a `vector(384)` column type and distance operators. `match_papers` returns your papers ordered by cosine similarity to a query vector ([`core/knowledge/embedding_service.py:51-57`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/embedding_service.py#L51-L57)).

The backend connects with the **service-role key** ([`backend/db/client.py:43-52`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/db/client.py#L43-L52)). That key ignores row-level security policies, so a query without `.eq('user_id', ...)` can read every user's data. Every repository method filters by user; when you write a new query, so must you.

### Primer: the frontend's two module-level stores

*standard · 4 min*

**In short:** Pages read through `useQuery`, backed by a module-level cache that outlives components; the processing tray reads a module-level job store that polls the API. Both are plain modules subscribed to with `useSyncExternalStore`.

In most React apps, a page fetches data into its own `useState` and loses it when you navigate away. Here, two kinds of data live in ordinary JavaScript modules instead, and components subscribe to them.

**The query cache** (`lib/query.js`) maps keys like `summaries|<id>` to responses, keeps at most 64 entries for 5 minutes, and shares one in-flight request between callers asking for the same key ([`frontend/src/lib/query.js:31-46`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/query.js#L31-L46)). `useQuery(key, fetcher)` is the hook pages use. Going from Timeline to Explore and back costs no request.

**The job store** (`lib/processingStore.js`) holds your recent jobs and polls `GET /api/process/jobs`: every 2 seconds while one runs, every 6 while one is queued, never when nothing is active ([`frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js:96-101`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js#L96-L101)). The tray in the layout shows it on every page.

A cache that outlives the page brings two rules:

1. Every change to data must call `invalidate(prefix)`. When a job succeeds, the store clears `summaries`, `corpus` and `graph` ([`frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js:79-92`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js#L79-L92)).
2. Every session change must clear everything, or the next person to sign in on that browser sees the previous user's library from memory ([`frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx:29-39`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx#L29-L39)).

Forget rule 1 and the page shows stale data until the TTL runs out.

> **Checkpoint:** You add a button that deletes a collection, but the dashboard keeps showing the old count after you navigate back. What is missing?
> - A useEffect that refetches on mount
> - A call to invalidate() for the affected key prefix after the delete
> - A longer DEFAULT_TTL
> - A new route on the backend
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>A call to invalidate() for the affected key prefix after the delete. The cache outlives the page by design; mutations must clear what they change ([`frontend/src/lib/query.js:154-169`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/query.js#L154-L169)).</details>

## The map

### The architecture: two halves meeting at a table

*core · 5 min*

**In short:** A layered FastAPI app (routes, services, repositories) and a pipeline package (`core/`) share one process and meet at the `processing_jobs` table.

The backend has two halves that you can learn separately.

**The web half** (`backend/`) is layered: routes handle HTTP, services hold rules, repositories talk to Supabase. `main_app.py` is the only place that wires them together ([`backend/main_app.py:1-11`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L1-L11)). The auth path follows the layers cleanly: route, `AuthService`, `UserRepository` ([`backend/services/auth_service.py:61-71`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/auth_service.py#L61-L71)).

**The pipeline half** (`core/`) knows nothing about HTTP. `pipeline/` turns PDFs into sections, `agents/` runs ten extractors in phases, `graph/` is the LangGraph summary engine, `llm/` builds the provider chain, `knowledge/` and `intelligence/` serve the on-demand features.

**They meet at a table.** Enqueue routes insert `processing_jobs` rows. `JobWorker`, started inside each API process at boot ([`backend/main_app.py:118-131`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L118-L131)), claims rows and calls `run_processing`, the service that runs the pipeline and saves the result.

The layering is not followed everywhere. The graph, corpus and intelligence routes call Supabase directly through a shared module-level client ([`backend/routes/knowledge_graph.py:9-21`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/knowledge_graph.py#L9-L21)), and so does the processing service ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:40`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L40)). Treat 'routes, services, repositories' as the direction new code should take, not as a description of all old code.

Redis is optional at every point where it appears; each feature that uses it falls back to per-process memory.

> **Checkpoint:** You need a new endpoint that returns a user's papers grouped by year. Following the intended layering, where does the grouping logic go?
> - In the route function, next to the Supabase query
> - In a service, with the query in a repository method
> - In core/knowledge
> - In the React page
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>In a service, with the query in a repository method. Routes stay thin, services hold rules, repositories hold queries ([`backend/main_app.py:8-10`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L8-L10)).</details>

### A tour of the folders

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** `backend/` is the web app, `core/` the pipeline, `frontend/src/` the React app, `evals/` the quality harness. The dependency map shows routes depending on core, and nothing in core depending on routes.

Walk the tree in this order:

- `backend/main_app.py`: the app factory. Start here.
- `backend/routes/`: one file per feature area, 15 files. `process_jobs.py` is what the app calls to process papers; `process_paper.py` is the old synchronous version, kept for scripts.
- `backend/services/`: `paper_processing_service.py` (the pipeline body) and `job_queue.py` (the worker) matter most.
- `backend/repositories/`, `backend/db/`: Supabase access.
- `backend/api/`: plumbing shared by all routes: errors, rate limits, caches, health, middleware.
- `backend/main.py`: 1,276 lines of the original extractors, still imported as fallbacks ([`core/agents/structure_agent.py:22`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/structure_agent.py#L22)).
- `core/pipeline/`, `core/agents/`, `core/graph/`, `core/llm/`: the processing path, in that order.
- `core/knowledge/`, `core/intelligence/`, `core/memory/`: on-demand features and cross-paper memory.
- `frontend/src/`: `App.jsx` routes, `pages/` (13), `components/`, `lib/` (client and stores), `contexts/` (auth, theme, toasts).
- `evals/`: the golden set and the benchmark.

The scanner's dependency map below agrees with the intended direction: `backend/routes` depends on `core` 15 times, and `core` reaches into `backend` only through two legacy modules, `backend.main` and `backend.database.config` ([`core/agent_integration.py:84-91`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agent_integration.py#L84-L91)).

The most-imported file in the repo is the frontend's design-system kit, `components/ui/primitives.jsx`, used by 30 files.

## Core ideas

### Failure is recorded, never dressed up as a result

*core · 4 min*

**In short:** Every stage records `ok` or `failed`, a summary that is empty, a placeholder or under 60 words is refused at save time, and an ungraded summary stores a null score. Expect failed jobs rather than thin summaries.

The idea that explains most of the defensive code in this repo: **a broken result must never look like a real one.** Earlier versions stored template text when the LLM was down, showed 'No tables detected' when table extraction had crashed, and wrote a made-up quality score of 0.6 when the judge failed. Each of those is fixed the same way: make the failure visible as data.

Three mechanisms, from the inside out:

1. **Per-stage status.** The orchestrator records each parallel agent as `ok` or `failed` with the error, and gives table extraction its own entry ([`core/agents/orchestrator.py:183-219`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L183-L219)). It is saved as `summary_data.pipeline_status`, so the UI can say 'this step failed' instead of 'nothing here'.
2. **No fake numbers.** When the grading call fails, the grade is stored as `graded: False` with `score: None`, which becomes a null `quality_score` column ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:532-539`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L532-L539)).
3. **The save gate.** Before the row is written, `_reject_degenerate_summary` refuses an empty summary, one that starts with a known placeholder sentence, or one under 60 words ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:531-570`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L531-L570)). The job then fails with a reason such as `summary_too_short`, visible in the tray.

Analogy: a lab that writes 'sample contaminated' on the label instead of guessing a value. Where it stops working: the summary graph's own last resort is to return the paper's abstract as the summary when every synthesis call fails ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:461-467`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L461-L467)), and an abstract over 60 words passes the gate. That is real text from the paper, not invented, but it is not a summary either.

> **Checkpoint:** During a Groq outage a job fails with `summary_too_short`. A colleague suggests lowering `_MIN_SUMMARY_WORDS` to 10 so users get something. What does the codebase's design say?
> - Good idea: any text beats a failed job
> - No: a short summary under rate limits is the failure mode the gate exists to catch; the job should fail and be retried
> - Only lower it for arXiv papers
> - Move the check to the frontend
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>No: a short summary under rate limits is the failure mode the gate exists to catch; the job should fail and be retried. The gate's own comment calls a short summary 'a failure wearing a summary's clothes' ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:526-528`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L526-L528)).</details>

### Jobs, leases and heartbeats

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** A job is a row. A worker claims it with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, holds a 900-second lease, renews it every 300 seconds, and abandons the run without writing if renewal fails.

Several Uvicorn processes may run, each with its own worker, and none of them shares memory with the others. All coordination happens in Postgres.

**Claiming.** `claim_processing_job` picks the next queued row and locks it with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`: a second worker asking at the same moment skips the locked row and takes the next one, so no job runs twice. It also refuses to give one user more than 2 running jobs ([`backend/config/settings.py:85-90`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L85-L90)). Fencing is enforced on every write: updates filter on `claimed_by = this worker` ([`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:97-103`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L97-L103)).

**Waiting before claiming.** The worker acquires its semaphore (1 slot by default) before it claims, so jobs it cannot start yet stay `queued` in the database where everyone can see them ([`backend/services/job_queue.py:96-102`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L96-L102)).

**The lease.** A claim sets `lease_expires_at` 900 seconds out. While the pipeline runs, a heartbeat renews it every 300 seconds. If a renewal returns false, the claim function has already handed the job to someone else; the run is cancelled and nothing is saved ([`backend/services/job_queue.py:177-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L177-L185)).

**Endings.** Success or duplicate finishes the job. Failure calls `fail_for_retry`, which requeues while `attempts < max_attempts` (2) ([`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:131-159`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L131-L159)). Shutdown releases the job immediately instead of waiting out the lease.

Analogy: a library book on hold with a due date. Keep renewing and it is yours; stop, and the desk gives it to the next person.

> **Checkpoint:** A worker's heartbeat reports the lease was lost halfway through a run. What does the worker do?
> - Saves the summary anyway, since the work is done
> - Cancels the run and writes nothing; the job's new owner finishes or fails it
> - Retries the heartbeat until it succeeds
> - Marks the job failed
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Cancels the run and writes nothing; the job's new owner finishes or fails it. Writing now could race another worker's insert for the same paper ([`backend/services/job_queue.py:177-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L177-L185)).</details>

### Agents, phases and the message bus

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Ten agents extend `BaseAgent` and run in four phases. They share a message bus for questions to each other, but no agent reads its mailbox, so those questions always time out.

An **agent** here is a class with one job, such as 'find entities' or 'parse ablation tables', and one async method, `process(input) -> dict`. `BaseAgent.execute` wraps it with timing and turns any exception into a result with an `error` key, so one broken agent cannot crash the run ([`core/agents/base_agent.py:160-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/base_agent.py#L160-L185)).

The orchestrator runs them in phases:

1. **Structure** alone: PDF to sections. If it fails, the run stops.
2. **Seven at once** on those sections: entity, results, figure, reasoning, research gap, ablation, reproducibility ([`core/agents/orchestrator.py:164-181`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L164-L181)).
3. ResultsAgent **again**, now with the entities, then ComparisonAgent.
4. **SummaryAgent**, which hands everything to the LangGraph engine.

With the graph engine on (always, today), the regex EntityAgent and ResultsAgent outputs are replaced by the graph's own extraction when the result is reshaped ([`core/agent_integration.py:166-178`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agent_integration.py#L166-L178)). They still run and still cost time.

The **message bus** was meant to let agents check each other: ResultsAgent asks EntityAgent whether a dataset name is known ([`core/agents/results_agent.py:233-244`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/results_agent.py#L233-L244)). Requests are routed into per-agent mailboxes, but nothing ever reads a mailbox, so every `ask_agent` waits its 3-second timeout and returns `None` ([`core/agents/base_agent.py:299-324`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/base_agent.py#L299-L324)). The docs mention conflicts 'resolved via voting'; `_cross_validate` only logs, and `consensus_votes` is always 0.

Read the bus as unfinished infrastructure, not as how the agents actually cooperate.

> **Checkpoint:** You are profiling a slow paper and see phase 3b take 30 seconds with no LLM calls. What is the most likely cause?
> - PyMuPDF re-reading the PDF
> - ResultsAgent asking EntityAgent about each unknown dataset and waiting 3 s per unanswered request
> - The Redis cache
> - The grade node retrying
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>ResultsAgent asking EntityAgent about each unknown dataset and waiting 3 s per unanswered request. Each unanswered `ask_agent` waits out `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=3.0)` ([`core/agents/message_bus.py:158-165`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/message_bus.py#L158-L165)), one result row after another.</details>

### The provider chain, tiers and budgets

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Every LLM call tries Gemini, then Groq, then Ollama, in a `fast` or `smart` size. The primary provider's character budget decides whether a paper is read in one call or section by section.

**Order.** `provider_order` builds the list. With `PAPERMIND_LLM_PROVIDER=auto` (the default) it includes Gemini if a Google key is set, Groq if a Groq key is set, and always Ollama, last. Naming a provider moves it first; `PAPERMIND_LLM_STRICT=1` drops the others ([`core/llm/providers.py:123-135`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L123-L135)).

**Tiers.** Each provider has a `fast` and a `smart` model: `gemini-flash-lite-latest` and `gemini-flash-latest`, Llama 3.1 8B and Llama 3.3 70B on Groq, Qwen 2.5 3B and 7B on Ollama ([`core/llm/providers.py:44-64`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L44-L64) = {]]). Section digests and extraction use `fast`; the single-pass read, synthesis and grading use `smart`.

**Fallback.** The graph wraps the chain with LangChain's `with_fallbacks`: an exception from one model, including a failed parse of structured output, moves on to the next. The Gemini and Groq clients also retry up to 6 times on their own and time out after 120 seconds ([`core/llm/providers.py:172-192`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L172-L192)).

**Budget.** How much text one request may carry depends on the primary: 400,000 characters for Gemini, 24,000 for Groq (its free tier meters about 6,000 tokens per minute), 12,000 for Ollama ([`core/llm/providers.py:68-84`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L68-L84)). A paper under the budget gets one `read_paper` call; over it, map-reduce. So the same paper can cost 3 calls with Gemini primary and about 16 with Groq primary.

**Pacing.** A global semaphore keeps at most `PAPERMIND_LLM_CONCURRENCY` (2) calls in flight, and `PAPERMIND_LLM_RPS` adds a requests-per-second cap.

The cost of silent fallback: a dead model name looks like a quality drop, not an error. `check_providers` and `run_meta.models_observed` exist to make it visible.

> **Checkpoint:** Only GROQ_API_KEY is set. A 40-page paper with 90,000 characters of text arrives. How is it read?
> - One read_paper call on Groq's smart model
> - Map-reduce, because 90,000 is over Groq's 24,000-character budget
> - Gemini, because it is always first
> - It is rejected for being too long
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Map-reduce, because 90,000 is over Groq's 24,000-character budget. Without a Google key Groq is primary, and `prepare` compares the paper with its budget ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:239-245`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L239-L245)).</details>

### Grounding claims: numbers first, similarity second

*deep · 5 min*

**In short:** The `verify` node checks up to 24 findings and contributions against the paper's own sentences: a claim with a number is supported only if the number appears in the paper; otherwise cosine similarity of 0.45 decides.

After the summary is accepted, `verify` takes up to 24 key findings and contributions and checks each against the cleaned sections, with the bibliography removed so a claim cannot match the title of a cited paper ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:583-601`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L583-L601)).

`verify_claims` splits the paper into sentences, embeds them and the claims with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and for each claim ([`core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py:153-183`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py#L153-L183)):

1. **Numeric rule.** Pull the numbers out of the claim, ignoring years 1900-2099. If there are any, the claim is grounded only if every one appears somewhere in the paper. A missing number is named in `unsupported_numbers`.
2. **Semantic rule.** With no informative number, the claim is grounded if its best sentence match has cosine similarity of at least 0.45.
3. **Unverifiable.** If embedding fails or there is no source text, `grounded` is `None`, never `True`.

Why two rules: on labelled claims, similarity alone scored close negatives at chance. '...reaches 28.4 BLEU' and '...reaches 31.7 BLEU' embed almost identically ([`core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py:30-40`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py#L30-L40)). Before comparing, numbers are repaired: pymupdf4llm writes 28.4 as `28 _._ 4` ([`core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py:45-61`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py#L45-L61)).

Known limits: a correct number the summary derived (a difference, a mean) is flagged; spelled-out numbers and flipped claims pass. On the single labelled paper, precision is 0.533.

And one integration gap: these verdicts are returned by the graph but not saved with the summary (see Handle with care).

> **Checkpoint:** A finding says 'improves BLEU to 31.7 on WMT14' but the paper reports 28.4. Which rule decides, and how?
> - The semantic rule, which finds a 0.95 similarity and marks it grounded
> - The numeric rule: 31.7 does not appear in the paper, so grounded is false and 31.7 is listed as unsupported
> - Neither; it is marked null
> - The grade node rejects it
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The numeric rule: 31.7 does not appear in the paper, so grounded is false and 31.7 is listed as unsupported. A claim with an informative number is decided by the numeric rule before similarity is consulted ([`core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py:77-92`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py#L77-L92)).</details>

## How it flows

### What happens when you upload a paper

*core · 8 min*

**In short:** Follow one PDF from the drop zone to a saved summary: enqueue, claim, extract, agents, summary graph, duplicate check, save gate, insert, post-save tasks, and the poll that tells the browser.

This is the main path through the system. Step through it below with the code open; here is the shape and the places it can stop.

**In the request (under a second).** The page checks the file type and the 50 MB limit, then posts it ([`frontend/src/pages/HomePage.jsx:107-134`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/pages/HomePage.jsx#L107-L134)). The route repeats the checks, verifies the `%PDF-` header and the 200-page limit, refuses a 21st open job, and answers 409 if the same bytes are already in your library. It saves the file as `uploads/jobs/<job id>.pdf`, inserts the job row and answers 202.

**In the worker (minutes).** A worker claims the row and runs `run_processing` against a heartbeat. It looks up the PDF's SHA-256 in Redis; on a miss, the orchestrator runs StructureAgent, seven agents in parallel, ResultsAgent again, ComparisonAgent and SummaryAgent, whose LangGraph engine writes the summary. Figures are uploaded to storage before the result is cached, so a cache hit never points at deleted temp files ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:297-306`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L297-L306)).

**Before saving.** An embedding of title, abstract and keywords is compared with your library; 0.95 or more makes the job `duplicate`. The save gate rejects degenerate summaries. The insert makes up to 4 attempts on network errors.

**After saving.** Your corpus caches are cleared, top-10 similarity rows written, citations and lineage inferred (only on the legacy extractor path today), entity pairs and analysis rows stored. These run before the job is marked done, so the dashboard is current when the tray says Done ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:224-231`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L224-L231)).

**Back in the browser.** The next poll sees `succeeded`, clears the `summaries`, `corpus` and `graph` caches and shows a toast.

Where it stops: a validation 4xx in the request; `failed` with a reason code in the worker (`pipeline_error`, `too_many_pages`, `summary_too_short`, `save_failed`); or `duplicate`.

**Flow: Upload a PDF and get a summary** (trigger: You drop a PDF on the home page while signed in.)

1. **The page checks the file and hands it to the job store** [`frontend/src/pages/HomePage.jsx:107-134`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/pages/HomePage.jsx#L107-L134) Rejects non-PDFs and files over 50 MB before any upload, then shows upload progress while `enqueueUpload` runs.
2. **The job store posts the file and shows it at once** [`frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js:201-205`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js#L201-L205) `jobs.enqueueUpload` sends multipart form data to `POST /api/process/jobs` with the default 30-second timeout ([`frontend/src/lib/api.js:237-248`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L237-L248)). The returned job is inserted into the store and polling starts.
3. **The route validates and rejects duplicates** [`backend/routes/process_jobs.py:120-142`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/process_jobs.py#L120-L142) Checks the extension, the 50 MB limit and the `%PDF-` magic bytes, refuses with 429 when you already have 20 open jobs, and answers 409 if a paper with the same SHA-256 is already in your library.
4. **The route stages the file and writes the job row** [`backend/routes/process_jobs.py:144-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/process_jobs.py#L144-L185) The PDF is saved as `uploads/jobs/<job id>.pdf` and a row with `dedupe_key = sha256:...` is inserted. A unique index turns a second identical enqueue into a 409. The response is 202 with the job.
5. **A worker claims the job** [`backend/services/job_queue.py:94-127`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L94-L127) Each Uvicorn process runs one `JobWorker`. It takes a semaphore slot first, then calls the `claim_processing_job` function, which picks the next queued row with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and caps each user at 2 running jobs. With nothing to do it sleeps 3 seconds plus jitter.
6. **The run races its own heartbeat** [`backend/services/job_queue.py:152-187`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L152-L187) The pipeline runs as one task and a heartbeat that renews the 900-second lease every 300 seconds runs as another. If a renewal fails, the pipeline is cancelled and nothing is saved.
7. **The pipeline body starts, using the cache when it can** [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:269-307`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L269-L307) `run_processing` checks the 200-page limit, reports stage `extracting`, and looks up the PDF's SHA-256 in Redis. On a miss it runs the agents, uploads figures, and caches the result for 24 hours, but only if it would pass the save gate.
8. **The orchestrator runs the agents in phases** [`core/agents/orchestrator.py:143-181`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L143-L181) StructureAgent extracts sections first. Seven agents then run at once on those sections; an exception in one becomes a `failed` entry in `stage_status` instead of stopping the run.
9. **StructureAgent turns the PDF into sections** [`core/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py:841-885`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py#L841-L885) `extract_pdf` tries pymupdf4llm (and MinerU when enabled), keeps the first backend that finds 3 or more sections, and falls back to plain PyMuPDF. Tables, title and authors are added afterwards in `_enrich_result`.
10. **SummaryAgent runs the summary graph** [`core/agents/summary_agent.py:94-111`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/summary_agent.py#L94-L111) The agent is a thin wrapper: it calls the LangGraph engine (traced in the next flow) and raises if no summary came back, which the orchestrator records as a failed stage.
11. **The result is reshaped into the stored format** [`core/agent_integration.py:158-178`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agent_integration.py#L158-L178) `_transform_to_legacy_format` flattens the agents' outputs into one dict. When the graph engine ran, its entities and results replace the regex agents' output.
12. **Near-duplicates are caught by embedding** [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:125-155`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L125-L155) The title, abstract and keywords are embedded and compared with your library; a match at 0.95 cosine or above makes the job `duplicate` instead of saving a second copy.
13. **The save gate checks the summary, then the row is inserted** [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:183-206`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L183-L206) `_build_summary_record` runs the save gate first; a rejected summary becomes a failed outcome with a reason such as `summary_too_short`. The insert makes up to 4 attempts on transport errors, waiting 1, 2 and 4 seconds between them.
14. **Post-save tasks fill the graph tables** [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:399-454`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L399-L454) Stage `analysing`: clear your cached corpus views, write top-10 similarity rows, citations and lineage (only when a `__references__` section exists), entity pairs, stored intelligence and GitHub links. Each step logs and continues on failure.
15. **The worker records the outcome** [`backend/services/job_queue.py:207-222`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L207-L222) `succeeded` and `duplicate` finish the job with the summary id; `failed` goes to `fail_for_retry`, which requeues it while attempts remain (2 by default).
16. **The next poll sees the change and refreshes the UI** [`frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js:79-101`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/processingStore.js#L79-L101) The store polls every 2 seconds while a job runs and every 6 while one is queued. On `succeeded` it clears the `summaries`, `corpus` and `graph` caches and shows a toast.

> **Checkpoint:** A user reports that an upload sat in 'Saving' for a long time and then showed Done. Which code ran between Saving and Done?
> - The LangGraph synthesis
> - The insert with retries, then the post-save tasks (similarity, citations, entities, intelligence)
> - The table subprocess
> - The frontend upload progress bar
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>The insert with retries, then the post-save tasks (similarity, citations, entities, intelligence). `saving` is set just before the record is built and inserted; `analysing` covers `_post_save_tasks` ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:157-231`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L157-L231)).</details>

### Inside the summary graph

*core · 7 min*

**In short:** `prepare` measures the paper; one `read_paper` call or the map-reduce branch produces digests, entities and results; `synthesize` writes the summary; `grade` may send it back once; `verify` grounds the findings.

SummaryAgent is a wrapper; the summarising happens in `core/graph/summary_graph.py`. Read `get_summary_graph` first: its 30 lines are the control flow ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:637-658`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L637-L658)).

**prepare** drops references, acknowledgements and stub sections, trims a bibliography glued to the last section, orders what is left by importance (abstract, introduction, method, results, ...) and measures it against the primary provider's budget ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:221-264`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L221-L264)).

**read_paper** (single pass) sends the full text and the tables in one `smart` call and gets back entities, results and a digest per section. If that call fails it returns `single_pass: False` and the graph falls through to map-reduce instead of losing the paper.

**map_sections, extract_entities, extract_results** (map-reduce) digest up to 24 sections concurrently on the `fast` tier; a section whose call fails keeps 600 raw characters, flagged `degraded`. The two extract nodes then run in parallel.

**synthesize** asks for the full `PaperSynthesis` with a ceiling of 8,192 output tokens. If the model leaves `key_findings` empty, they are filled from result rows ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:471-476`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L471-L476)).

**grade** scores faithfulness and specificity. A score under 0.6 with fewer than 2 attempts loops back to `synthesize` with the judge's issues appended. Scores on a 0-5 or 0-10 scale are rescaled. A judge that fails twice marks the summary ungraded.

**verify** grounds up to 24 claims and never fails the run.

Each LLM call is recorded (model that answered, tokens, seconds) and the run gets a prompt fingerprint ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:686-691`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L686-L691)).

**Flow: Inside the summary graph: from sections to a graded, checked summary** (trigger: SummaryAgent calls `run_graph_summary` during phase 4 of the pipeline.)

1. **The adapter builds the graph's input** [`core/graph/adapter.py:40-62`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/adapter.py#L40-L62) Pulls sections, the domain, the title from page-1 metadata, and the tables as Markdown out of the orchestrator's input.
2. **A run recorder starts and the graph is invoked** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:664-691`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L664-L691) `start_run` puts a recorder in a context variable so token counts from concurrent papers do not mix; the compiled graph is cached after the first build.
3. **prepare cleans the paper and picks a strategy** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:221-264`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L221-L264) Drops references, acknowledgements and stubs under 120 characters, orders sections by importance, and compares the paper's length with the primary provider's budget.
4. **The budget comes from the primary provider** [`core/llm/providers.py:80-96`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L80-L96) 400,000 characters for Gemini, 24,000 for Groq, 12,000 for Ollama; `PAPERMIND_LLM_CONTEXT_CHARS` overrides it.
5. **Single pass: one call reads the whole paper** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:271-308`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L271-L308) Returns entities, results and a digest of every section in one structured response. If it fails, it sets `single_pass` to false and the graph falls through to map-reduce.
6. **Map-reduce: one call per section, then two extractions in parallel** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:326-362`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L326-L362) Up to 24 sections, 12,000 characters each, on the fast tier. A failed section keeps its first 600 raw characters, flagged `degraded`. `extract_entities` and `extract_results` then run side by side ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:648-653`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L648-L653)).
7. **Every call goes through the provider chain** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:140-157`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L140-L157) Builds the chain for the tier, wraps it in `with_fallbacks`, and holds a semaphore (2 calls by default). Total failure returns `None` rather than raising, and the caller decides what that means.
8. **synthesize writes the summary** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:429-476`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L429-L476) One smart-tier call fills `PaperSynthesis`: an 800-1200 word analysis, method and setup sections, contributions, findings, limitations, future work. On a retry it includes the grader's list of issues.
9. **grade judges it and may send it back once** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:498-564`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L498-L564) Under 150 words scores 0 without a call. Otherwise an LLM judge scores it; below 0.6 with fewer than 2 attempts loops to `synthesize`. A failed judge marks the summary ungraded and accepts it.
10. **verify checks each finding against the paper** [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:575-611`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L575-L611) Up to 24 findings and contributions go to `verify_claims` with the cleaned sections, so a claim cannot match the bibliography ([`core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py:114-117`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py#L114-L117)).
11. **The adapter shapes the result for the agents** [`core/graph/adapter.py:105-139`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/adapter.py#L105-L139) Returns `summaries.main`, findings and the rest, plus `claims`, `grade` and `run_meta`. The next step, `_transform_to_legacy_format`, does not copy `claims` or `run_meta`, so those are dropped before saving (see Handle with care).

> **Checkpoint:** The grade node returns a score of 7.5 for a summary. What does the graph do?
> - Retries, because 7.5 is not between 0 and 1
> - Rescales 7.5 to 0.75 (it is over 5, so divide by 10), which passes the 0.6 bar
> - Marks the summary ungraded
> - Fails the run
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Rescales 7.5 to 0.75 (it is over 5, so divide by 10), which passes the 0.6 bar. Weak models answer on other scales; [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:543-549`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L543-L549) normalises before the routing decision.</details>

### Opening a paper's knowledge graph

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** The Graph tab fetches the paper's graph and recommendations through the cache; the server builds nodes and edges from your 80 newest papers, the similarity rows written at save time, and each paper's stored entities.

Nothing is computed when you open the tab except assembly. The expensive part, similarity, was done when each paper was saved: `compute_and_cache_similarity` asked `match_papers` for the 10 closest library papers at 0.3 or above and stored them in `paper_similarity` ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:51-73`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L51-L73)).

At view time, `get_knowledge_graph`:

1. reads your 80 newest summaries, selecting only `summary_data->entities` from the JSON column;
2. loads similarity pairs at 0.5 or above whose both ends are in that set;
3. keeps the anchor paper and its neighbours (or everything, if the anchor is older than your newest 80);
4. adds an entity node only if the anchor mentions it or more than one visible paper does ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:253-288`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L253-L288)).

The docstring records an earlier version that read entities from the global `entity_relationships` table and showed other users' entities on everyone's graph ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:172-179`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L172-L179)). Reading from your own `summary_data` fixed that.

On the client, d3-force lays out the nodes and every mark is SVG coloured from theme tokens. Recommendations come from a separate route that reads `paper_similarity` for this paper; it does not check that the paper is yours, and it only finds papers older than this one.

**Flow: Open a paper's knowledge graph** (trigger: On a summary page you click the Graph tab.)

1. **Switching to the tab triggers a lazy load** [`frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx:441`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx#L441) Graph data is not fetched until you open the tab.
2. **Two cached requests run in parallel** [`frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx:212-227`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx#L212-L227) Keys `graph|paper|<id>` and `graph|recs|<id>` go through `fetchQuery`, so a second visit within 5 minutes costs no request.
3. **The client calls the graph routes** [`frontend/src/lib/api.js:259-261`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L259-L261) `GET /api/graph/paper/{id}` and `GET /api/graph/recommendations/{id}`.
4. **The route runs the builder off the event loop** [`backend/routes/knowledge_graph.py:24-39`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/knowledge_graph.py#L24-L39) Calls `get_knowledge_graph` in a thread with your user id and the paper as the anchor; any exception becomes a 500 with the message.
5. **Your newest 80 papers are read, entities only** [`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:184-198`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L184-L198) The `->` selector pulls one key out of the JSONB column, so whole summaries never cross the wire.
6. **Similarity edges are loaded** [`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:200-210`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L200-L210) Only pairs scoring 0.5 or more, both ends in the set, up to 200 rows. These rows were written at save time by `compute_and_cache_similarity`.
7. **The anchor's neighbourhood is chosen** [`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:212-221`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L212-L221) The paper plus every paper it shares a similarity edge with. If the paper is not among your newest 80, the whole set is shown instead.
8. **Entity nodes are added only when they connect something** [`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:253-288`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L253-L288) An entity appears if the anchor mentions it or more than one visible paper does, with a `mentions` edge to each paper.
9. **The browser lays out and draws the graph** [`frontend/src/components/KnowledgeGraph.jsx:218-229`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/components/KnowledgeGraph.jsx#L218-L229) d3-force places nodes; every mark is SVG coloured from theme tokens, so dark mode works without extra code.

> **Checkpoint:** Recommendations for the first paper you ever uploaded are always empty, even though later papers are similar to it. Why?
> - d3-force hides isolated nodes
> - Similarity rows are written once, from each new paper to older ones, and recommendations only read rows where this paper is paper_a
> - The browser cache is stale
> - The embedding model was not loaded
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Similarity rows are written once, from each new paper to older ones, and recommendations only read rows where this paper is paper_a. Rows are written with the new paper as `paper_a_id` ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:64-73`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L64-L73)) and recommendations filter on it ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:81-95`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L81-L95)). The graph view reads both directions, so the paper still has neighbours there.</details>

### Signing in and staying signed in

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Login checks a bcrypt hash, returns a 24-hour HS256 JWT in the body and as an httpOnly cookie, and the browser keeps the body copy in localStorage and sends it as a Bearer header.

The login route is rate-limited to 10 calls per minute per caller and hands off to `AuthService.login` ([`backend/auth/routes.py:59-70`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/routes.py#L59-L70)). The service lower-cases the email, loads the user, and checks the password with bcrypt in a thread. When the email does not exist it still runs bcrypt against a fixed dummy hash, so the response takes the same time either way and cannot be used to discover registered emails ([`backend/services/auth_service.py:31-34`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/auth_service.py#L31-L34)).

A match produces a JWT signed with HS256 and `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, carrying `user_id`, `email`, `iat` and an expiry 24 hours ahead. The route returns it in the JSON body **and** sets it as an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie ([`backend/auth/routes.py:28-42`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/routes.py#L28-L42)).

The browser uses the body copy: `applySession` clears every cached response, saves the token in localStorage and starts the job poller ([`frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx:72-80`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx#L72-L80)). An axios interceptor adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to each request. On the server, `get_current_user` prefers the header and falls back to the cookie.

On reload, AuthContext decodes the stored token's expiry locally before calling `/api/auth/me`, so a dead token costs no request ([`frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx:41-70`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx#L41-L70)). Any 401 clears the token and caches and redirects to `/login?next=...`.

Two things to know: the token in localStorage is readable by any script on the page, and logout only deletes the cookie, so a copied token works until it expires.

**Flow: Sign in and stay signed in** (trigger: You submit the login form.)

1. **AuthContext calls the login endpoint** [`frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx:82-92`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx#L82-L92) On success the response goes to `applySession`; on failure the error message is returned to the form.
2. **The client posts the credentials** [`frontend/src/lib/api.js:166-167`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L166-L167) `POST /api/auth/login` with email and password.
3. **The route applies the auth rate limit** [`backend/auth/routes.py:59-70`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/routes.py#L59-L70) `@limit('auth')` allows 10 per minute per caller, then `AuthService.login` does the work.
4. **The service checks the password in constant time** [`backend/services/auth_service.py:105-127`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/auth_service.py#L105-L127) An unknown email still runs bcrypt against a dummy hash, so response time does not reveal which emails exist. Inactive accounts get 403.
5. **A token is signed** [`backend/auth/utils.py:39-47`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/utils.py#L39-L47) HS256 over `user_id`, `email`, `iat` and an expiry 24 hours out ([`backend/config/settings.py:43-45`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L43-L45)).
6. **The token is also set as a cookie** [`backend/auth/routes.py:28-42`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/routes.py#L28-L42) httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, and `secure` only in production so local HTTP still works.
7. **The browser stores the session** [`frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx:72-80`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx#L72-L80) Clears every cached response first (they belonged to the previous user), saves the token in localStorage and starts the job poller.
8. **Every request carries the token** [`frontend/src/lib/api.js:72-78`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L72-L78) An axios request interceptor adds the header.
9. **Protected routes decode it** [`backend/auth/dependencies.py:14-41`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/dependencies.py#L14-L41) The Bearer header wins over the cookie. A missing, expired or invalid token raises `AuthenticationError`, which the error handler turns into a 401.
10. **A 401 ends the session everywhere** [`frontend/src/lib/api.js:94-109`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L94-L109) Clears the token and the cache and sends you to `/login?next=...`. LoginPage does not read `next`, so you land on the dashboard.

### Simulating a peer review

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** An on-demand LLM call outside the pipeline: ownership check, cache check, a reviewer prompt built from the stored summary, one call at temperature 0.15, a validated score card cached in `paper_intelligence`.

The intelligence features follow one pattern, and peer review shows it end to end.

The route first checks you own the paper and returns a cached review unless `force=true` ([`backend/routes/intelligence.py:212-243`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/intelligence.py#L212-L243)). The agent builds its context only from keys the pipeline really saves: the original abstract or the main summary, the method and setup write-ups, up to 20 result rows, contributions, findings and limitations. Under 200 characters of context it refuses with `PeerReviewUnavailableError` rather than letting the model invent weaknesses ([`core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py:130-135`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py#L130-L135)).

The call goes through `LocalLLM.generate`, which tries the shared provider chain first ([`core/llm/llm_interface.py:371-381`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/llm_interface.py#L371-L381)), at temperature 0.15 so the same paper does not flip between accept and reject. The answer must contain all four scores (novelty, soundness, clarity, significance); a recommendation that contradicts the mean score is corrected; the result is upserted into `paper_intelligence`.

Three details: the client allows 180 seconds for this call; the stored `llm_backend` is the configured primary, not necessarily the provider that answered ([`core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py:157-164`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py#L157-L164)); and the button passes its click event as `force`, so every click regenerates and spends a call.

**Flow: Simulate a peer review** (trigger: On a summary's Intelligence tab you click Simulate peer review.)
