1. **The button calls the handler** [`frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx:153-167`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx#L153-L167) Calls the API, then reloads the stored intelligence for the paper. The button passes its click event as `force`, so every click regenerates ([`frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx:1000`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/pages/SummaryPage.jsx#L1000)).
2. **The client allows 180 seconds** [`frontend/src/lib/api.js:305-311`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L305-L311) `ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT` covers one LLM round trip; `force=true` goes as a query parameter.
3. **The route checks ownership and the cache** [`backend/routes/intelligence.py:212-243`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/intelligence.py#L212-L243) 404 if the paper is not yours; returns a cached review unless `force`. `PeerReviewUnavailableError` becomes 503.
4. **The agent builds the reviewer's context from summary_data** [`core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py:87-135`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py#L87-L135) Abstract, method, setup, results, contributions, findings and limitations, each truncated. Under 200 characters in total it refuses rather than invent a review.
5. **One LLM call goes through the shared chain** [`core/llm/llm_interface.py:371-381`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/llm_interface.py#L371-L381) `LocalLLM.generate` tries the Gemini, Groq, Ollama chain first and only then its own per-backend clients.
6. **The review is validated, reconciled and stored** [`core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py:150-178`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/peer_review_agent.py#L150-L178) All four scores must be present; a recommendation that contradicts the mean score is corrected; the result is upserted into `paper_intelligence` with `analysis_type = peer_review`.

## Data and state

### The data model: one wide row per paper

*core · 5 min*

**In short:** `summaries` holds one row per paper per user, with the full pipeline output in the `summary_data` JSONB column and a 384-dimension embedding. `processing_jobs` is the queue; similarity, citations, lineage and intelligence tables hang off summaries.

If you learn one table, learn `summaries`. Its columns are few: owner, title, authors, arXiv id, the upload's SHA-256, model used, timing, word count, quality score, embedding. Almost everything else is inside `summary_data`, whose shape is defined in one function, `_build_summary_record` ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:573-630`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L573-L630)):

- `summaries.main`, `methods_detail`, `experimental_setup`: the prose;
- `key_findings`, `contributions`, `limitations`, `future_work`: lists;
- `entities`, `typed_entities`, `models`, `datasets`, `metrics`, `tasks`;
- `results.metrics`: rows of metric, value, model, dataset, is_best;
- `tables`, `figures` (with storage URLs), `section_summaries`, `sections_found`;
- `research_gaps`, `ablation_studies`, `reproducibility`;
- `pipeline_status`: per-stage `ok` or `failed`.

Adding a field is a code change only: write it in `_build_summary_record`, read it in the frontend. No migration. The flip side is that no schema checks the two sides agree.

`processing_jobs` is the second table to know: its `status` moves through queued, running and a terminal state, and `stage` through extracting, saving and analysing ([`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:105-129`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L105-L129)).

The rest are written after a save (`paper_similarity`, `paper_citations`, `paper_lineage`, `entity_relationships`, `paper_github_links`) or on demand (`paper_intelligence`). All of them reference a summary id.

In this checkout the SQL files are deleted, so the diagram below was rebuilt from the committed SQL and the code; run `git checkout HEAD -- backend/database` to read the originals.

> **Checkpoint:** You want to store a new 'datasets_used_with_licenses' list from the graph engine. What do you change?
> - Write a migration adding a column to summaries
> - Add the key in _build_summary_record (and carry it through the adapters), then read it in the frontend
> - Create a new table
> - Add it to processing_jobs
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Add the key in _build_summary_record (and carry it through the adapters), then read it in the frontend. `summary_data` is JSONB; its shape is whatever [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:587-621`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L587-L621) writes.</details>

### Four caches and what clears them

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Pipeline results by PDF hash in Redis for 24 hours, corpus views per user for 5 minutes, responses in the browser for 5 minutes, and rate-limit buckets. Each has its own invalidation rule.

Stale data in this app almost always comes from one of four caches.

**1. The processing cache** (`core/pipeline/processing_cache.py`). Key: `papermind:pdf:v2:<sha256 of the PDF>`; TTL 24 hours ([`core/pipeline/processing_cache.py:42-52`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/pipeline/processing_cache.py#L42-L52)). A byte-identical PDF skips the whole pipeline. Only results that pass the save gate are cached, and figures are uploaded before caching. When a pipeline change makes old entries wrong, bump `_CACHE_VERSION`; that is how the figure fix retired every broken entry. If Redis is down, it remembers that and stops trying ([`core/pipeline/processing_cache.py:19-22`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/pipeline/processing_cache.py#L19-L22)).

**2. The corpus view cache** (`backend/api/response_cache.py`). Topic clusters, citation network and similar views per user, 5 minutes ([`backend/api/response_cache.py:35`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/api/response_cache.py#L35)). Every write path calls `invalidate_user(user_id)` ([`backend/api/response_cache.py:135-158`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/api/response_cache.py#L135-L158)). Without Redis it is per process, so with 2 workers the other process can serve a stale view for up to 5 minutes.

**3. The browser query cache** (`frontend/src/lib/query.js`). 64 entries, 5 minutes, keys like `summaries|<id>`. `invalidate('summaries')` clears every key under that prefix, and also drops in-flight requests so a reply to an old request cannot write stale data back.

**4. Rate-limit buckets** (`backend/api/rate_limit.py`). Not data, but state: a token count per caller in Redis or in process memory.

When a user says 'I uploaded it but it is not in Explore', check 2 and 3 in that order.

> **Checkpoint:** You fix a bug in how tables are extracted. Users re-uploading an old PDF still see the broken tables. What else must you change?
> - Clear the browser cache
> - Bump _CACHE_VERSION in processing_cache.py so cached pipeline results from before the fix are not reused
> - Lower the Redis TTL
> - Restart Uvicorn
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Bump _CACHE_VERSION in processing_cache.py so cached pipeline results from before the fix are not reused. A cache hit returns the stored result without running extraction ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:281-286`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L281-L286)).</details>

### How the graph tables get filled

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** After each save: up to 10 similarity rows, then citations and two kinds of lineage (only when a `__references__` section exists), then entity pairs, intelligence rows and GitHub links. RelationAgent can add typed lineage later on request.

`_post_save_tasks` runs five steps in order, and each one logs and carries on if it fails ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:399-454`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L399-L454)).

1. **Similarity.** `match_papers` returns library papers at cosine 0.3 or more; the top 10 become `paper_similarity` rows from the new paper to each older one.
2. **Citations and lineage.** The bibliography is parsed, matched to arXiv ids already in your library, and stored in `paper_citations` (up to 100). Matched citations become `cites` lineage rows; similar papers at 0.75 or more become `inspired_by` rows ([`core/knowledge/lineage_service.py:52-88`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/lineage_service.py#L52-L88)). This whole step only runs if a section is named `__references__`, a name only the legacy extractor produces.
3. **Entity pairs.** Up to 50 entities, paired, upserted into `entity_relationships` with columns `entity_a`/`entity_b` that the experience store's code does not use.
4. **Intelligence.** Research gaps, reproducibility and ablations found by the pipeline agents go into `paper_intelligence`, one row per type.
5. **GitHub links.** Repositories found by ReproducibilityAgent are looked up and stored with stars and activity.

Separately, `POST /api/corpus/relate-papers` runs RelationAgent over pairs in your library and writes typed links (extends, replicates, contradicts, ...) into `paper_lineage` ([`core/graph/schemas.py:108-117`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/schemas.py#L108-L117)).

Note the direction of `inspired_by`: the new paper is written as the ancestor of the older one.

## File by file

### Backend files to open first

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Open `main_app.py`, then the processing trio (`process_jobs.py`, `job_queue.py`, `paper_processing_service.py`), then the plumbing in `backend/api/` and the repositories.

Read the backend in three passes.

**Pass 1, the spine.** `main_app.py` shows every router and middleware in one screen ([`backend/main_app.py:62-98`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main_app.py#L62-L98)). Then `config/settings.py` for every knob with its default: limits, timeouts, queue sizes ([`backend/config/settings.py:57-94`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L57-L94)).

**Pass 2, the processing trio.** `routes/process_jobs.py` (what a request may enqueue), `services/job_queue.py` (who runs it, with what lease), `services/paper_processing_service.py` (what running means, and what gets saved). Together they are about 1,400 lines and cover most production incidents.

**Pass 3, the plumbing.** `api/errors.py` gives every `AppError` one JSON shape, `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}` ([`backend/api/errors.py:87-93`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/api/errors.py#L87-L93)). `api/rate_limit.py` is the token bucket. `api/deps.py` builds repositories and services per request. `repositories/base.py` runs every Supabase call in a thread and wraps driver errors as `RepositoryError`, which renders as 503 `storage_unavailable`.

Skip on the first read: `backend/main.py` (legacy extractors, imported only as fallbacks), `routes/process_paper.py` (deprecated synchronous processing) and the smaller feature routers (annotations, collections, reading queue, feedback, export), which are thin CRUD.

The cards below say when to open each file and what will surprise you in it.

### Pipeline files to open first

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** Follow the processing order: `agent_integration.py`, `orchestrator.py`, `structure_agent.py` and `pdf_extractor.py`, then `summary_graph.py` with `schemas.py`, then `providers.py`.

`core/` is easiest to read in the order a paper moves through it.

1. `agent_integration.py`: the entry from the service, and the function that decides the stored shape ([`core/agent_integration.py:122-133`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agent_integration.py#L122-L133)).
2. `agents/orchestrator.py`: the phases. Read `process_paper` top to bottom once ([`core/agents/orchestrator.py:127-155`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L127-L155)).
3. `agents/structure_agent.py` and `pipeline/pdf_extractor.py`: how a PDF becomes sections. The backend chain and `_enrich_result` are the parts to understand; the figure-rendering helpers can wait.
4. `pipeline/table_extractor.py`: only the subprocess part at first, to know why it exists.
5. `graph/summary_graph.py` with `graph/schemas.py` open beside it: every prompt string sits in the first file, and every field description in the second is sent to the model too.
6. `llm/providers.py`: the chain and the budgets.

Of the other agents, open one (EntityAgent or ResultsAgent) to see the pattern, then skip the rest until you need them; with the graph engine running, their entity and result output is replaced anyway.

`llm/llm_interface.py` is the older text interface used by the intelligence agents. It now routes through `providers.py` first ([`core/llm/llm_interface.py:371-381`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/llm_interface.py#L371-L381)), so you can treat `providers.py` as the one LLM layer and `LocalLLM` as an adapter.

### Frontend files to open first

*standard · 4 min*

**In short:** `App.jsx` for routes, `lib/api.js` for every endpoint, `lib/query.js` and `lib/processingStore.js` for the two stores, `AuthContext.jsx` for sessions, then `HomePage.jsx` and `SummaryPage.jsx`.

The frontend has 13 pages, but you can work on most of it after reading five files.

- `App.jsx`: the route table. Every page except home, login, signup and the two password pages is wrapped in the auth guard ([`frontend/src/App.jsx:49-58`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/App.jsx#L49-L58)).
- `lib/api.js`: the only HTTP client and a named function for every endpoint. Timeouts live here: 30 seconds by default, 180 for single LLM calls, 600 for the deprecated pipeline routes ([`frontend/src/lib/api.js:42-62`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/frontend/src/lib/api.js#L42-L62)). If you add a route that calls an LLM, give it an explicit timeout.
- `lib/query.js` and `lib/useQuery.js`: the cache every page reads through.
- `lib/processingStore.js`: the job poller behind the tray.
- `contexts/AuthContext.jsx`: session start, restore and end.

Then the two big pages. `HomePage.jsx` is the upload and arXiv search. `SummaryPage.jsx` is 1,244 lines: the summary plus Entities, Figures, Tables, Graph and Intelligence tabs, each loaded lazily the first time you open it.

The design system is `components/ui/primitives.jsx` (Button, Card, Badge, Tabs, Bento grid, ScrollArea), imported by 30 files. Use it rather than styling from scratch.

Before pushing UI changes run `npm run lint` and, with the dev server and API up, `npm run smoke`: lint and build both pass on code that crashes the moment it renders.

### Knowledge, intelligence and eval files

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** `graph_service.py` and `embedding_service.py` build similarity and graphs; `hallucination_guard.py` grounds claims; `peer_review_agent.py` is the template for on-demand analysis; `golden_eval.py` and `label.py` are the quality gate.

These files are off the main processing path, except one.

**Knowledge.** `embedding_service.py` loads all-MiniLM-L6-v2 once per process and calls the `match_papers` function for vector search. `graph_service.py` writes similarity rows after a save and assembles graph payloads at read time. `lineage_service.py` writes and reads `paper_lineage` for the timeline and ancestry views. `paper_search.py` searches Semantic Scholar and falls back to arXiv for Discover and for state-of-the-art suggestions.

**Intelligence.** `hallucination_guard.py` is the exception: it runs inside the summary graph on every paper. `peer_review_agent.py` is the cleanest example of an on-demand feature: build context from `summary_data`, refuse when it is too thin, one LLM call, validate, cache.

**Memory.** `experience_db.py` wraps the cross-paper tables (entity knowledge, metric baselines, pattern hit rates, agent run logs) that agents query to raise or lower confidence. These tables have no `user_id`; they are shared across all users by design.

**Evals.** `label.py` builds a golden-set file by extracting a paper and pre-filling a stub from the paper's own text, never from PaperMind's output. `golden_eval.py` scores grounding precision and recall, section detection, numeric fidelity and degenerate rate, and `gate` fails CI below the floors in `thresholds.json` ([`evals/golden_eval.py:477-503`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/evals/golden_eval.py#L477-L503)). The set holds one paper today, so treat its numbers as a worked example.

## How it was built

### How the project grew

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** A Flask prototype (Nov 2025), a 7-agent v2 on Supabase (Apr 2026), the LangGraph engine (Jun 2026), a layered FastAPI rewrite with Docker (Aug 2026), background jobs and an eval gate (late Aug 2026), and fresh-clone fixes (Oct 2026).

22 commits, one developer, eleven months. The commit messages from August onward are long and specific; when you wonder why something is odd, `git log -p` on that file usually answers it.

The story in five turns:

1. **A prototype** (Nov 2025): a Flask app and the font-based extractors that still live in `backend/main.py` ([`backend/main.py:168-206`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main.py#L168-L206)).
2. **v2** (`3165199`, Apr 2026): seven agents in parallel, pgvector similarity, lineage, collections, and the move to Supabase.
3. **The LangGraph engine** (`43c6018`, Jun 2026) replaced a summariser that read about the first 4,000 characters and extracted entities by regex ([`core/graph/summary_graph.py:1-4`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L1-L4)). The first benchmark (`42259d9`) then found figures silently dropping to zero per paper.
4. **Layering and Docker** (`010cf6b`, `60ed5a5`, Aug 2026): the Flask app deleted, `backend/api/` added for errors, rate limits, middleware and health, a redesigned frontend, Compose.
5. **Honesty** (`d58caf1`, `a75250b`, late Aug 2026): processing moved to background jobs; silent failures in figures, tables and grading fixed; the grounding guard wired in; the golden-set gate added. Commit `a75250b` opens with 'The pipeline was unmeasured, ungrounded and unobservable.'

The last batch (29 Oct 2026) fixes what only a fresh clone exposes, such as a `.gitignore` rule for Python's `lib/` that also hid `frontend/src/lib/` ([`.gitignore:15-16`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/.gitignore#L15-L16)).

Most commits since April carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer.

> **Checkpoint:** You find `werkzeug` in backend/requirements.txt even though the app is FastAPI. What is the likeliest explanation?
> - FastAPI requires it
> - A leftover from the Flask era; it is still used for `secure_filename` on uploads
> - It powers the rate limiter
> - It is a test dependency
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>A leftover from the Flask era; it is still used for `secure_filename` on uploads. The upload route imports it for one helper ([`backend/routes/process_jobs.py:31`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/process_jobs.py#L31)); the Flask app was deleted in `010cf6b`.</details>

### If you rebuilt it: the order to build in

*deep · 5 min*

**In short:** Settings and health first; persistence and auth; PDF extraction; one structured LLM call; the summary graph; agents around it; the processing service; the job queue; the frontend; knowledge and evals last.

The milestones below follow the import graph: files that many others depend on come first, and pages that nothing imports come last. Each one ends with something you can run.

Three lessons from the history are worth building in from the start rather than retrofitting:

- **Make failure a value.** `ProcessingOutcome` has `status`, `error_code` and `error_message` ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:77-89`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L77-L89)); agents return error dicts; stages record `ok` or `failed`. Every one of these replaced a path where an error became an empty list.
- **Queue from day one.** The job table replaced a request that held a connection open for minutes. A queue changes the API shape (202 plus polling), which is cheap early and expensive later.
- **Measure before trusting.** The benchmark found the zero-figures bug on its first run, and the golden set found the grounding guard had no production call site.

If you rebuild with fewer moving parts, the strongest candidates to drop are the message bus (no agent reads its mailbox) and the regex Entity and Results agents (their output is replaced when the graph engine runs).

## Why it's like this

### The decisions behind the design

*standard · 6 min*

**In short:** Ten decisions explain most of the code: background jobs in Postgres, no template fallback, single-pass reading, the free-tier chain, pgvector and JSONB, tables in a subprocess, a Lua token bucket, numeric-first grounding, adapters that keep the old shape, and caches that outlive pages.

Most decisions here are **documented**: the code says why, in a docstring or a commit message, usually with the incident that caused it. The records below quote that evidence. One is marked **inferred**, where the reasoning is ours.

A pattern runs through them: the project optimises for **free-tier LLM limits** and for **never mistaking a failure for a result**.

- Free tiers explain single-pass reading (fewer requests), the provider chain (no single provider stays up), the concurrency semaphore, the request-rate cap, and the per-user queue caps ([`backend/config/settings.py:85-90`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L85-L90)).
- Honest failure explains the save gate, null quality scores, per-stage status, the table subprocess returning its own error, and the numeric grounding rule.

When you face a design choice, ask both questions: does this spend more requests per paper, and could its failure look like a normal result? The existing code answers them consistently, and reviewers will ask them.

The trade-offs are real. The worker shares the API process, so one CPU-heavy extraction slows requests on that process. The two adapters keep old consumers working, at the price of new fields being lost unless threaded through both.

> **Checkpoint:** Someone proposes calling the LLM once per section for every paper 'for consistency'. Which existing decision does that undo, and why was it made?
> - The Redis cache; it was for speed
> - Single-pass reading; free tiers limit requests more tightly than context, and one call that sees the whole paper can tie table numbers to methods
> - JSONB storage; it was for migrations
> - The token bucket; it was for fairness
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Single-pass reading; free tiers limit requests more tightly than context, and one call that sees the whole paper can tie table numbers to methods. See [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:24-28`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L24-L28).</details>

### Why the queue is a table and the worker lives in the API

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** Postgres already provides locking (`SKIP LOCKED`), durability and per-user queries, so a table plus an asyncio worker replaced a Celery plan with no new service. The cost is CPU sharing with the API.

The v2 commit added a Celery and Redis task queue; it did not survive. The current design uses what was already running:

- **Postgres as the queue.** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` gives each worker a different row without a lock manager. A partial unique index on `(user_id, dedupe_key)` for active jobs makes 'already queued' a constraint violation instead of a check-then-insert race ([`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:22-29`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L22-L29)).
- **asyncio as the worker.** One `JobWorker` per Uvicorn process, a semaphore for concurrency, a heartbeat task for the lease ([`backend/services/job_queue.py:1-20`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L1-L20)). No broker, no separate deployment.
- **Room to split later.** Staged files are named by job id, not by the uploaded filename, so a future worker container mounting the same volume can find them ([`backend/routes/process_jobs.py:147-152`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/process_jobs.py#L147-L152)), and Compose carries a commented-out `workers` profile.

The trade-off is stated in the settings: extraction is CPU-bound and shares the process with the API, and the shared free-tier quota is the real bottleneck, so concurrency is 1 job per process ([`backend/config/settings.py:80-84`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L80-L84)). With 2 Uvicorn workers that is 2 papers at a time for the whole deployment.

This choice is **documented** in the module docstrings and commit `d58caf1`.

> **Checkpoint:** You run 4 Uvicorn workers with the default settings. How many papers can be processing at once, and what stops one user from taking all of them?
> - 1, because Postgres locks the table
> - 4 (1 per process); claim_processing_job caps each user at 2 running jobs
> - Unlimited; the semaphore is per request
> - 20, the per-user queue cap
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>4 (1 per process); claim_processing_job caps each user at 2 running jobs. `job_concurrency` is per process and `job_max_per_user` is enforced in the claim ([`backend/config/settings.py:80-90`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/config/settings.py#L80-L90)).</details>

## Handle with care

### Where to be careful

*core · 5 min*

**In short:** The biggest gaps: grounding verdicts are computed but not saved; upload retries cannot succeed; citations run only on the legacy extractor path; two graph routes skip ownership checks; the session token sits in localStorage.

Every item below was found by reading the code, and each risk card points at the exact lines. Severity is our judgement.

**Grounding is computed, then dropped (high).** The `verify` node checks every finding and the adapter returns `claims` and `run_meta` ([`core/graph/adapter.py:94-103`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/adapter.py#L94-L103)). `_transform_to_legacy_format` copies a fixed list of keys and neither of those is in it, and `_build_summary_record` has no `claims` key. No code reads `summary_data.claims`. The README says the verdicts are stored. Until fixed, the eval gate measures a guard whose output users never see.

**Upload retries cannot succeed (medium).** The worker deletes the staged PDF in `finally` before `fail_for_retry` requeues the job, so attempt 2 has no file ([`backend/services/job_queue.py:199-205`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L199-L205)).

**Citations and lineage are usually skipped (medium).** They need a section named `__references__`, which only the legacy extractor creates ([`backend/main.py:267-270`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/main.py#L267-L270)).

**Two routes trust any paper id (medium).** Recommendations and ancestry query by id with the service-role key and no owner filter.

**A rejected insert hangs the job (medium).** A PostgREST error escapes `run_processing`, and the job stays `running` until its 15-minute lease runs out.

The full list, with advice, is below. The two exercises that fix the first two items are good first contributions.

> **Checkpoint:** A reviewer asks you to show a 'verified' badge next to each key finding. What do you need to change first?
> - Nothing; summary_data.claims already holds the verdicts
> - Carry `claims` through `_transform_to_legacy_format` and `_build_summary_record` so it is saved at all
> - Lower SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD
> - Add a new LLM call in the frontend
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>Carry `claims` through `_transform_to_legacy_format` and `_build_summary_record` so it is saved at all. The verdicts exist only in memory today; [`core/agent_integration.py:303-318`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agent_integration.py#L303-L318) and [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:587-621`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L587-L621) do not include them.</details>

### Code that runs but does nothing

*standard · 5 min*

**In short:** Unanswered agent questions, a voting step that never votes, a write to `entity_relationships` with the wrong columns, unused helpers in SummaryAgent, and a settings flag nothing reads.

These cost time or mislead readers without causing visible errors.

**Agent questions nobody answers.** Agents send requests over the bus; messages land in mailboxes no agent reads; each request waits 3 seconds and returns `None` ([`core/agents/base_agent.py:403-405`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/base_agent.py#L403-L405) has no callers). ResultsAgent sends one per result row with an unknown dataset, in sequence.

**Voting that never votes.** `_cross_validate` only logs, and `consensus_votes` is initialised to 0 and never changed ([`core/agents/orchestrator.py:303-344`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L303-L344)).

**A write that cannot match its table.** `_persist_entities` upserts `entity_a`, `entity_b`, `source_paper_id` ([`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:375-391`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L375-L391)) into the table the experience store reads as `entity_1`, `entity_2` ([`core/memory/experience_db.py:347-353`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/memory/experience_db.py#L347-L353)). The failure is caught and logged.

**Unused helpers.** `SummaryAgent` keeps `_get_section`, `_build_paper_context` and `_score_quality` from before it became a wrapper; nothing calls them ([`core/agents/summary_agent.py:38-71`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/summary_agent.py#L38-L71)).

**A flag nothing reads.** `PAPERMIND_USE_GRAPH` is declared in settings and set in Compose, and `.env.example` says it turns the graph on, but the graph is the only path and no code checks the flag.

**Work replaced afterwards.** With the graph engine on, EntityAgent and ResultsAgent run and their entities and results are then discarded in favour of the graph's.

Before deleting any of these, search the tests in a full checkout: some may be exercised there.

> **Checkpoint:** You see 'entity_persist_failed' in the logs after every paper. Is the paper's knowledge graph affected?
> - Yes, the graph has no entities
> - No; the graph reads entities from each paper's summary_data, not from entity_relationships
> - Yes, similarity edges are missing
> - Only for arXiv papers
>
> <details><summary>Answer</summary>No; the graph reads entities from each paper's summary_data, not from entity_relationships. `get_knowledge_graph` selects `summary_data->entities` ([`core/knowledge/graph_service.py:184-198`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/graph_service.py#L184-L198)); the docstring explains why it stopped using `entity_relationships`.</details>

### Security notes

*standard · 4 min*

**In short:** The service-role key bypasses row-level security, so every query must filter by user; two graph routes do not. The token sits in localStorage, logout does not revoke it, and rate-limit rules share one bucket.

**Ownership is the code's job.** The backend connects with the service-role key ([`backend/db/client.py:43-52`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/db/client.py#L43-L52)), which ignores Postgres row-level security. Repositories filter by `user_id` on every query, and the intelligence routes call `_check_paper_ownership` first ([`backend/routes/intelligence.py:51-69`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/routes/intelligence.py#L51-L69)). `GET /api/graph/recommendations/{id}` and `GET /api/graph/ancestry/{id}` do not: they accept any id.

**Tokens.** The JWT is returned in the body and stored in localStorage, where any script on the page can read it, and also set as an httpOnly cookie. Logout deletes the cookie; the token itself stays valid for 24 hours. There is no revocation list.

**Good practices already in place.** Login runs bcrypt against a dummy hash for unknown emails to avoid revealing which accounts exist. Passwords over 72 bytes are rejected because bcrypt would silently truncate them ([`backend/auth/utils.py:63-74`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/auth/utils.py#L63-L74)). Job responses never include the server file path. Production refuses a wildcard CORS origin and a placeholder JWT secret.

**Rate limits.** The bucket key is the caller only, so `auth`, `upload` and `expensive` rules draw from one stored token count with different capacities ([`backend/api/rate_limit.py:315-316`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/api/rate_limit.py#L315-L316)). `/api/health?probe_llm=true` needs no login and makes a real call to each provider.

**HTML output.** The slide export pastes the paper title, authors and LLM text into HTML without escaping ([`core/intelligence/slide_generator.py:94-105`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/slide_generator.py#L94-L105)). The deck is downloaded as a file rather than shown in the app, which limits the damage, but escape it before ever rendering it in the page.

### When the docs disagree with the code

*deep · 3 min*

**In short:** README, CLAUDE.md and `.env.example` lag the code in a few places: the worker, the graph flag, the graph renderer, and where grounding results are stored. This checkout is also missing its tests and SQL.

The docs in this repo are unusually good, which makes the few stale spots easy to trust by mistake. Known gaps:

- The README's deployment section says processing runs inside the request and 'There is no worker service' ([`README.md:471-472`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/README.md#L471-L472)). Since `d58caf1` it runs in a background `JobWorker`.
- `.env.example` says the graph engine is off unless `PAPERMIND_USE_GRAPH=1` and suggests `gemini-2.0-flash` model overrides ([`backend/.env.example:31-49`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/.env.example#L31-L49)); the flag is not read, and `providers.py` says that model now returns 404.
- CLAUDE.md describes `KnowledgeGraph.jsx` as vis-network ([`CLAUDE.md:196`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/CLAUDE.md#L196)); it is d3-force.
- CLAUDE.md lists four parallel agents ([`CLAUDE.md:282-286`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/CLAUDE.md#L282-L286)); the orchestrator runs seven.
- The README says grounding verdicts land in `summary_data.claims`; they are not saved.

**About this checkout.** `git status` shows `tests/` (35 files), `backend/database/*.sql` (17 files), `setups/`, `scripts/backfill.py` and `TODO.md` deleted but not committed. A fresh clone has them. This guide cites only files on disk, so the schema is described from the code that uses it. CI's `pytest tests/` would fail on this working copy as it stands.

Rule of thumb: when a doc and the code disagree, the code is right about what happens; the commit log is usually right about why.

## Your first changes

### Your first changes

*core · 3 min*

**In short:** Seven real changes, from a one-line UI fix to making upload retries work. The first two take minutes; numbers 4 and 7 fix the two most serious gaps in this guide's risk list.

Pick by what you want to learn:

- **The job lifecycle:** exercise 1 (show the Fetching stage) and exercise 7 (make upload retries work). Together they take you through the worker, the repository and the tray.
- **The frontend:** exercise 2 (the peer-review button) is one line and teaches how React passes event arguments.
- **Quality and prompts:** exercise 3 (move the grounding threshold) needs no API key and teaches the eval loop.
- **The data path:** exercises 4 (save the grounding verdicts) and 5 (citations on the default extractor) both require threading a value through the adapters into `summary_data`. They are the most useful changes in this list.
- **The API plumbing:** exercise 6 (one rate-limit bucket per rule) with a unit test.

For each, the card lists the files and a test of done. Run the relevant check before you open a PR: `pytest` for backend changes, `npm run lint` and `npm run smoke` for frontend changes, `python evals/golden_eval.py score` for anything touching prompts, schemas or the guard.

### How to change a prompt safely

*deep · 4 min*

**In short:** Prompts are the strings in `summary_graph.py` and the field descriptions in `schemas.py`. Change one, re-run the golden-set score, compare the prompt fingerprint, and never lower a threshold to pass.

A prompt change is invisible to unit tests, so this repo treats it like a model change.

1. **Find the prompt.** System and user messages are string literals inside the node functions of `summary_graph.py`. The output contract is `schemas.py`, and its field descriptions are sent to the model; the module says they 'materially affect extraction quality' ([`core/graph/schemas.py:14-15`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/schemas.py#L14-L15)).
2. **Change one thing.** Keep field order in `PaperReading` as it is: short fields first, or long `sections` output uses up the token budget.
3. **Check the fingerprint moved.** `prompt_fingerprint()` hashes the schemas and the source of the six prompt-building nodes; your change should give a new 12-character value ([`core/graph/provenance.py:206-215`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/provenance.py#L206-L215)).
4. **Score it.** `python evals/golden_eval.py score` needs no key for grounding and section detection. With saved predictions (`--predictions`) it also scores numeric fidelity, headline recall and degenerate rate.
5. **Respect the floors.** `thresholds.json` holds floors with the measured value and a reason. Raise one when a metric improves; never lower one to turn CI green.

Also probe the providers (`/api/health?probe_llm=true`) before blaming a prompt: a retired model in the chain looks exactly like a worse prompt.

### Glossary

- **Job**: A row in `processing_jobs` that says 'please process this paper for this user'. [`backend/repositories/job_repository.py:22-47`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/repositories/job_repository.py#L22-L47)
- **Lease and heartbeat**: A worker that claims a job holds it for 900 seconds and renews that hold every 300 seconds. [`backend/services/job_queue.py:152-163`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/job_queue.py#L152-L163)
- **Agent**: A class with one async `process(input)` method that extracts one kind of thing from a paper. [`core/agents/base_agent.py:101-185`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/base_agent.py#L101-L185)
- **Orchestrator phases**: Structure first, then seven agents at once, then comparison, then the summary. [`core/agents/orchestrator.py:143-181`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L143-L181)
- **Sections**: The paper as a dictionary from a heading-derived name (`introduction`, `model_architecture`) to that section's text. [`core/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py:125-131`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/pipeline/pdf_extractor.py#L125-L131)
- **Single pass and map-reduce**: If the whole paper fits the provider's budget, one LLM call reads all of it; if not, each section is summarised separately and the pieces are combined. [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:239-245`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L239-L245)
- **Structured output**: Asking the LLM to fill in a Pydantic class instead of writing free text. [`core/graph/schemas.py:1-16`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/schemas.py#L1-L16)
- **Provider chain and tiers**: An ordered list of LLM providers to try, in two sizes: `fast` for per-section work, `smart` for the final write-up. [`core/llm/providers.py:123-135`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/llm/providers.py#L123-L135)
- **Grade**: A second LLM call that judges the summary for faithfulness and specificity and may trigger one rewrite. [`core/graph/summary_graph.py:532-539`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/summary_graph.py#L532-L539)
- **Grounding**: Checking each key finding against the paper's own sentences: true (supported), false (unsupported) or null (could not check). [`core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py:153-169`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/intelligence/hallucination_guard.py#L153-L169)
- **Save gate**: The last check before a summary is stored: empty, placeholder or under-60-word summaries are rejected as failures. [`backend/services/paper_processing_service.py:531-570`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/backend/services/paper_processing_service.py#L531-L570)
- **pipeline_status**: A per-stage `ok` or `failed` record saved with each summary. [`core/agents/orchestrator.py:183-219`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/agents/orchestrator.py#L183-L219)
- **Embedding**: 384 numbers that place a paper's title, abstract and keywords in space so similar papers sit close together. [`core/knowledge/embedding_service.py:36-42`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/embedding_service.py#L36-L42)
- **Lineage**: Directed links from an older paper to a newer one: it cites it, it was inspired by it, or RelationAgent labelled the pair. [`core/knowledge/lineage_service.py:15-37`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/knowledge/lineage_service.py#L15-L37)
- **Prompt fingerprint**: A 12-character hash of every schema and prompt-building function, recorded with each run. [`core/graph/provenance.py:181-224`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/graph/provenance.py#L181-L224)
- **Experience store**: Cross-paper memory in Supabase: entities seen before, metric baselines, regex hit rates. [`core/memory/experience_db.py:69-80`](https://github.com/SanyamWadhwa07/PaperMind/blob/fcb26daddeb531fc05f07e845aabe419385b1e3f/core/memory/experience_db.py#L69-L80)
